Hey Cosimo - I'm not Spanish, so I can only answer some of your questions.

Israel theoretically should accept digital apostilles that are official and approved by the issuing country. However because they are not yet so common, there is a risk that PIBA staff may not know of how to handle them and they may want to send the documents to be checked by the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which may cause delays for your case. Therefore, you may want to consider to also issuing a physical apostille, if it's possible. Up to you.  

Regarding the multilingual version of the documents, from what I understand if the translation is in an annex (i.e., not on the face of the document itself) and if it is a translation to English (rather than Hebrew), it's very unlikely to be accepted. However others should correct me if they have experienced otherwise :)
